newsitem.title: USA: Empire State Bldg installs metal detectors.
newsitem.headline: Empire State Bldg installs metal detectors.

text.p: Metal detectors were installed at the Empire State Building on Monday as politicians pleaded for stronger U.S. gun controls one day after a distraught Palestinian man went on a deadly shooting spree on the world-famous skyscraper's observation deck.

A 69-year-old man identified by officials from his Palestinian Authority passport as Ali Abu Kamal opened fire just after 5 p.m. EST (2200 GMT) on Sunday, killing Danish rock band musician Christoffer Burmeister and wounding six others before shooting himself to death with a .038-calibre Beretta semiautomatic handgun.

Burmeister was a 27-year-old jazz guitarist for the Bush Pilots rock band. Matthew Gross, 29, of New Jersey, who played in the same band, was in critical condition with a gunshot wound to the head, a spokesman for Bellevue Hospital said.
Mario Carmona, 51, of Argentina, who was shot in the neck, and Jacob Schaad, 30, of Switzerland, who was shot in the chest, were both in serious but stable condition, the Bellevue spokesman said.

At St. Vincent's Hospital a married couple from Verdun, France, were in serious but stable condition in the intensive care unit. A 35-year-old man from the Bronx was in stable condition there, the hospital spokesman said on Monday night.

Building management for the skyscraper maintained that security was adequate before Sunday's apparently random attack but said it was taking the additional steps of installing baggage scanners and metal detectors so that all visitors to the 86th-floor observatory could be checked.

"The Empire State Building has excellent security 24 hours a day, seven days a week," general manager Steven Tole said. "The Empire State Building has been host to more than 95 million visitors without one serious incident."

He said the problem was "guns getting into the city, this is guns coming from Florida, this could have happened anywhere." The observation deck was closed on Monday and would reopen to visitors on Tuesday morning.

Mayor Rudolph Giuliani and gun control advocates bitterly decried the ease with which a foreign visitor to the United States could purchase a powerful gun. Kamal, who arrived in the country only on Dec. 24, bought the gun legally under Florida and federal laws but would have had to meet stricter identification and residential requirements in New York, Giuliani said.

New York Democratic Representative Carolyn McCarthy, who lobbied for gun control after her husband was shot to death and her son wounded on a commuter train in 1993, told reporters national gun laws had to be changed.

"New York State and New York City have great gun control laws but we cannot control all the guns that are coming in from other parts of the country and that's what has to be stopped," she said. "The time has come. It's an embarrassment to this country."

Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles defended his state against critics, who said the gunman was able to obtain the state ID card to buy the weapon at the end of January by checking into a cheap motel in Melbourne, Florida.

"It is far from true that the state is cavalier about its gun laws," Chiles said. Other Florida officials said that if Kamal bought the gun after being in the United States just three weeks, he either lied or the background checks failed at the federal level.
Police Commissioner Howard Safir told reporters that Kamal was a professor of English in Gaza who had suffered financial losses in which he felt he had been cheated out of his life savings.

"This caused him to be in a very depressed and emotional state," Safir said. "We are not discounting anything but at this point that particular scenario seems to fit better than any connection to a particular group or political organisation."

The widow of the gunman said on Monday in Gaza that her husband was not politically motivated but in despair over having been cheated out of $500,000. She said he travelled to the United States last December seeking a financier for a new investment company.

CBS Radio reported Monday night that an unnamed police source said that the Palestinian gunman carried a note that expressed his anger at the United States for using Israel as an instrument against Palestinians.
An official police department spokesman said they could not confirm the information.
The shooting was the worst bloodshed at the 102-story building since July 1945, when a B-25 bomber lost in fog crashed into the 79th floor, killing 14 people and injuring 26 others.
